{"id": "0d26eb14-9741-40d3-9fa5-4bb4115ac613", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's my review of this advanced event selector, evaluated purely on its logic (no account access, so I can't confirm it against the live trail or check if you have a separate selector for reads):

## Syntax — valid
Field names, casing, and operators check out against CloudTrail's schema: `eventCategory` and `resources.type` only support `Equals` (confirmed against docs — you're using it correctly), and `StartsWith`/`NotStartsWith` are valid for `resources.ARN`. The `scratch-bucket/` exclusion value correctly includes a trailing slash, so it won't accidentally also match something like `scratch-bucket-prod`. That's good hygiene.

## Issue 1 — This is a blocklist, not an allowlist (scope risk)
The selector has no `resources.ARN Equals/StartsWith` entry naming `finance-bucket` or `hr-bucket`. With only a `NotStartsWith` exclusion for `scratch-bucket/`, it defaults to matching **every S3 bucket in the account** — not just the three you listed. That means:
- Any bucket created in the future gets swept into this "audit" selector automatically.
- If the actual intent is "audit writes to finance-bucket and hr-bucket only," this configuration is broader than that intent and will generate (and bill for) data events on buckets outside your audit scope.

**Fix if you want to scope to just the two buckets:** drop the `NotStartsWith` and instead use
```
{Field: resources.ARN, StartsWith: [[redacted ARN], [redacted ARN]]}
```
That naturally excludes scratch-bucket (and anything else) without needing a blocklist at all — tighter scope, same outcome for these three buckets.

If account-wide-except-scratch is actually what you want, the current selector is fine as-is — just confirm that's the intent.

## Issue 2 — `eventName` list misses other write APIs
I confirmed against the S3/CloudTrail docs that `AWS::S3::Object` data events cover far more than `PutObject`/`DeleteObject`. Filtering to just those two means the following writes to finance/hr buckets would **not** be logged:
- `DeleteObjects` — the bulk/batch delete API (distinct from single-key `DeleteObject`)
- `CompleteMultipartUpload`, `CreateMultipartUpload`, `UploadPart`, `UploadPartCopy` — multipart uploads (common for larger files)
- `CopyObject` — writes via server-side copy
- `PutObjectTagging`, `PutObjectAcl`, `PutObjectRetention`, `PutObjectLegalHold`, `RestoreObject` — metadata/permission/compliance writes

If the audit goal is "capture all writes to these buckets," this is a real blind spot — bulk deletes and large multipart uploads in particular would slip through today.

## Summary
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Selector syntax/operators | ✅ Valid |
| ARN prefix precision | ✅ Good (trailing slash) |
| Bucket scope | ⚠️ Matches all buckets except scratch, not just finance+hr |
| Write coverage | ⚠️ Misses DeleteObjects, multipart upload APIs, CopyObject, tagging/ACL/retention writes |

Want me to draft a corrected selector with the allowlist approach and the expanded `eventName` list?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
